 Learn more Investing.com -- IDP Education (ASX:IEL) on Monday rejected a third takeover proposal from Blackstone, saying the revised A$3-per-share cash offer, which values the Australian education services company at A$833.7 million ($564.5 million), substantially undervalues its business.

 IDP said its board unanimously concluded that the proposal was opportunistic in its timing and not in the best interests of shareholders. The offer, submitted by Blackstone Singapore on behalf of funds managed by the investment firm, sought to acquire all outstanding shares through a recommended scheme of arrangement. 
 The board, advised by Goldman Sachs and legal adviser Mallesons, said the proposal did not adequately reflect IDP's position as a global student placement platform or the strategic value of its co-ownership of the IELTS English-language testing network.

 It also argued that Blackstone's offer failed to account for the potential financial benefits of its multi-year transformation programme, which has exceeded its fiscal 2026 targets and remains on track for its fiscal 2027 objectives. 
 Blackstone's latest proposal was 20% higher than its previous A$2.50-per-share offer and around 30% above its initial A$2.30 approach, both of which IDP had rejected. 
 The board said the latest offer came while the company's earnings were being significantly affected by student-visa restrictions across major destination markets. Although IDP expects market volumes to contract in fiscal 2027 compared with the previous year, it sees scope for student numbers to return to sustainable growth over the coming years. 
 IDP said the proposed transaction did not justify further engagement or granting Blackstone access to due diligence, which the board considered a distraction from managing the business. 
 The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) guidance of A$95 million to A$115 million, adding that year-to-date trading remained in line with expectations.
